claims.text: The identity of X (Si, Mn, or Al) controls protective-oxide formation and integrity in CrFeCoNiX alloys at high temperature.
Al- or Si-containing CrFeCoNiX preferentially forms a dual-layer oxide scale.
The proposed dual-layer scale has an inner Cr-rich, spinel-like region.
The proposed dual-layer scale has an outer passivating Al2O3 or SiO2 layer.
The Al2O3 or SiO2 outer layer has a thermal-expansion coefficient more closely matched to the underlying metallic phases.
The proposed composite scale grows slowly and remains coherent under high thermal stress.
The proposed composite scale resists cracking and spallation.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX forms a less chemically stable, more defect-rich, rapidly growing oxide scale.
The oxide scale on Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX is prone to cracking and spallation.
Al2O3 and SiO2 have low oxygen diffusivity and reduce oxide-growth stresses when present in the proposed scale.
Formation of thermodynamically stable Al2O3 or SiO2 together with a Cr-rich inner layer increases scale adhesion.
The Al- or Si-derived dual scale reduces thermal-expansion mismatch.
Higher adhesion and reduced thermal-expansion mismatch suppress rapid oxide growth and interfacial stress accumulation.
Suppressing oxide growth and interfacial stress prevents crack initiation and spallation.
Mn-containing alloys lack the proposed protective dual-scale effect and instead form more defective oxides.
Above 900 °C, Al- or Si-containing alloys will show less cracking, spallation, and oxide growth than Mn-containing alloys under otherwise identical exposure conditions.
CrFeCoNi without an added reactive element, or with Mn, does not promote formation of a highly adherent dual-layer oxide to the same extent as Al- or Si-modified CrFeCoNi.
The proposed behavior applies to single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution CrFeCoNiX exposed to oxidative or corrosive environments above 900 °C.
